'''Oscar Tshiebwe''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|ʃ|iː|b|w|eɪ}} {{respell|SHEEB|way}};{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=24 October 2023|access-date=17 May 2024}} born 27 November 1999) is a Congolese professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Houston Rockets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia Mountaineers]] and the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. In 2022, Tshiebwe was the [[List of U.S. men's college basketball national player of the year awards|consensus national player of the year]]. ==Early life== Tshiebwe grew up in [[Lubumbashi]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. He played [[soccer]] as a child but was encouraged to start [[basketball]] because of his above-average height.{{cite web |last=Hunter |first=Greg |title=WVU fans get a taste of Tshiebwe |url=https://www.wvnews.com/sports/wvu/wvu-fans-get-a-taste-of-tshiebwe/article_11808b79-7495-5feb-bb9d-ce646e8c1b89.html |publisher=WV News |access-date=10 July 2019 |date=24 December 2018}} Tshiebwe trained by running on hills and on a mountain near his hometown.{{cite web |last=White |first=Mike |title=Oscar Tshiebwe, Kennedy Catholic forward, is turning heads on the recruiting trail |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/high-school-basketball/2018/08/01/oscar-tshiebwe-recruiting-2019-class-west-virginia-kentucky-kennedy-catholic-pitt-basketball/stories/201808010157 |website=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] |access-date=10 July 2019 |date=1 August 2018}} He later attended a basketball camp led by Congolese NBA player [[Bismack Biyombo]], who helped advance his career.{{cite web |last=Squadron |first=Alex |title=Bigger than basketball: How Bismack Biyombo is creating change in the Congo |url=https://www.slamonline.com/nba/bigger-than-basketball-how-bismack-biyombo-is-creating-change-in-the-drc/ |website=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]] |access-date=10 July 2019 |date=6 May 2019}} Tshiebwe did not start playing basketball until May 2014. ==High school== Tshiebwe moved to the United States in November 2015,{{cite web |last=Everett |first=Brad |title=Kennedy Catholic junior Oscar Tshiebwe reaching elite status |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/hsother/2018/04/25/Kennedy-Catholic-junior-Oscar-Tshiebwe-recruiting-basketball/stories/201804250057 |website=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] |access-date=10 July 2019 |date=25 April 2018}} before his freshman year of high school, attending Mountain Mission School in [[Grundy, Virginia]]. Entering his junior year, he transferred to [[Kennedy Catholic High School (Hermitage, Pennsylvania)|Kennedy Catholic High School]] in [[Hermitage, Pennsylvania]].{{cite web |last=White |first=Mike |title=Kennedy Catholic basketball team is talented — and controversial |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/high-school-basketball/2018/08/01/oscar-tshiebwe-recruiting-2019-class-west-virginia-kentucky-kennedy-catholic-pitt-basketball/stories/201808010157 |website=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] |access-date=10 July 2019 |date=22 December 2017}} As a junior, Tshiebwe averaged 21.1 points per game and led his team to a [[Pennsylvania Interscholastic Athletic Association]] (PIAA) Class 1A title.{{cite web |title=Meet the District 10 Boys Basketball All-Stars |url=https://www.goerie.com/sports/20180406/meet-district-10-boys-basketball-all-stars |website=[[Erie Times-News]] |access-date=10 July 2019 |date=6 April 2018}} He earned Class 1A All-State first team honors.{{cite web |last=Groller |first=Keith |title=Becahi's Ryan Young, Moravian Academy's Jordan Holmqvist earn first-team honors |url=https://www.mcall.com/sports/varsity/mc-spt-all-state-boys-basketball-20180501-story.html |website=The Morning Call |access-date=10 July 2019 |date=1 May 2018}} In his senior season, Tshiebwe averaged 23.4 points, 18 rebounds, and five blocks per game, leading Kennedy Catholic to a 24–3 record and the PIAA Class 6A championship.{{cite web |title=KC's Tshiebwe named Gatorade Pa. Player of the Year |url=https://www.sharonherald.com/sports/kc-s-tshiebwe-named-gatorade-pa-player-of-the-year/article_b760c3a2-47a4-11e9-83cb-03912157005a.html |website=[[The Herald (Sharon)|The Herald]] |access-date=10 July 2019 |date=16 March 2019}}{{cite web |title=Meet the District 10 Boys Basketball All-Stars |url=https://www.goerie.com/sports/20190331/meet-district-10-boys-basketball-all-stars |website=[[Erie Times-News]] |access-date=10 July 2019 |date=31 March 2019}} He was a Class 6A All-State first team pick and was named Pennsylvania [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]].{{cite web |last=Groller |first=Keith |title=All-state boys basketball: Becahi's Justin Paz, Moravian Academy's Jordan Holmqvist earn first-team honors |url=https://www.mcall.com/sports/varsity/basketball/mc-spt-all-state-boys-basketball-20190514-nmqlnde3vzho3fs443xsgdvqbq-story.html |website=The Morning Call |access-date=10 July 2019 |date=14 May 2019}} He averaged 21.6 points, 11.8 rebounds, and 3.1 blocks per game playing for ITPS Wildcats Select on the Adidas Gauntlet. Tshiebwe played in the [[2019 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]] and [[Nike Hoop Summit]].{{cite web |last=Smith |first=Brad |title=Oscar Tshiebwe, McDonald's Kentucky 95-60 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/grady-tshiebwe-help-no-20-kentucky-rout-w-kentucky-95-60/ |access-date=22 December 2021}} At the close of the season, Tshiebwe was named the [[Sporting News Men's College Basketball Player of the Year|''Sporting News'' National Player of the Year]],{{cite news |last=DeCourcy |first=Mike |date=9 March 2022 |title=Kentucky's Oscar Tshiebwe is Sporting News' College Basketball Player of the Year |work=[[Sporting News]] |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/kentucky-oscar-tshiebwe-sporting-news-college-basketball-player-year/no1jcozbjgucugmkppdxp78u |access-date=9 March 2022}} as well as the unanimous [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Southeastern Conference Player of the Year]].{{cite news |last=Tipton |first=Jerry |date=8 March 2022 |title=SEC coaches name Kentucky's Oscar Tshiebwe their player of the year |newspaper=Lexington Herald-Leader |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article259181713.html |access-date=8 March 2022}}{{cite news |last=Zenor |first=John |date=8 March 2022 |title=Kentucky's Tshiebwe earns AP's SEC player of year honors |work=Associated Press News |url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-basketball-florida-arkansas-africa-820479dcffb7f4d4e2ac7314aabb46bf |access-date=8 March 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Indiana Pacers / Mad Ants (2023–2024)=== After going undrafted in the [[2023 NBA draft]], Tshiebwe joined the [[Indiana Pacers]] for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]]. On 3 July 2023, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Pacers, splitting time with their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Indiana Mad Ants]].{{cite web|title=Pacers Sign Tshiebwe and Wong to Two-Way Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-tshiebwe-and-wong-to-two-way-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=3 July 2023|access-date=6 September 2023}} On 9 December, he made his NBA debut in the [[2023 NBA In-Season Tournament championship game]] against the [[2023–24 Los Angeles Lakers season|Los Angeles Lakers]], and recorded his first regular-season point on 13 December, against the [[2023–24 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]]. On 18 February 2024, Tshiebwe was selected to the 2024 NBA G League Next Up Game, along with Mad Ants teammates [[Isaiah Wong]] and [[Kyle Mangas]], where his team was crowned champions. Tshiebwe also participated in the 2024 NBA [[Rising Stars Challenge]] at [[2024 NBA All-Star Game|All-Star Weekend]], where his team lost in the finals to MVP and Pacers teammate [[Bennedict Mathurin]]. On 2 April 2024, Tshiebwe was awarded the [[NBA G League Rookie of the Year Award]] after leading the league in rebounding and set a new NBA G League single-season rebounding record with 16.2 rebounds per game.{{cite web|title=Oscar Tshiebwe Named NBA G League's Rookie Of The Year For 2023-24|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/oscar-Tshiebwe-named-nba-g-league-rookie-of-the-year-for-2023-24|website=NBA.com|date=2 April 2024|access-date=2 April 2024}} In [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023–24]], he recorded 27 double-doubles, seven games with 20-plus points and 20-plus rebounds, broke the record for most rebounds collected in an [[Indiana Mad Ants]] season, and broke the Mad Ants record for most rebounds in a game with 28. He was also selected to the [[All-NBA G League Team|All-NBA G League 1st Team]], as well as the All-NBA G League Rookie Team.{{Cite web |last=East |first=Tony |date=2024-04-20 |title=Indiana Pacers two-way contract center Oscar Tshiebwe named to 2024 All-NBA G League First Team |url=https://www.si.com/nba/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-two-way-contract-center-oscar-tshiebwe-named-to-2024-all-nba-g-league-first-team#:~:text=INDIANAPOLIS%2520%25E2%2580%2594%2520Indiana%2520Pacers%2520rookie%2520center,as%2520the%2520All%252DRookie%2520Team. |access-date=2024-10-27 |website=SI.com |language=en-US}} ===Utah Jazz / Salt Lake City Stars (2024–2026)=== On 12 August 2024, Tshiebwe signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|first=Gabby|last=Hundman|title= Utah Jazz Sign Oscar Tshiebwe to Two-Way Contract|url= https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-oscar-tshiebwe-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=12 August 2024|access-date=12 August 2024}} On 28 March 2025, Tshiebwe made his first career start, recording seven points, 10 rebounds, one assist, and one steal in a 129-93 loss to the [[2024–25 Denver Nuggets season|Denver Nuggets]].{{Cite web|title=BBNBA: Oscar's first career start, Herro's 30-pieces, Davis's return|url=https://www.on3.com/teams/kentucky-wildcats/news/bbnba-oscars-first-career-start-herros-30-pieces-daviss-return/|access-date=April 20, 2025|website=on3.com|language=en}} He made 14 appearances (one start) for Utah during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 7.6 points, 8.7 rebounds, and 0.6 assists. On 19 August 2025, Tshiebwe re-signed with the Jazz on a two-way contract.{{Cite web |date=August 19, 2025 |title=Utah Jazz Sign Oscar Tshiebwe to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-oscar-tshiebwe-to-two-way-contract-2 |access-date=September 23, 2025 |website=nba.com |language=en}} On 10 April 2026, Tshiebwe put up 16 points and a career-high 22 rebounds in a 147–101 win over the [[2025–26 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/utah-jazz/jazz-news-the-insane-triple-double-history-made-in-tank-off-vs-grizzlies|title=The insane triple-double history made in egregious tank-off Jazz vs. ===Personal life=== Tshiebwe is a [[Christian]].{{cite web |last=Doering |first=Joshua |title=Oscar Tshiebwe, nation's leading rebounder, thankful for God's guidance in journey to Kentucky |url=https://sportsspectrum.com/sport/basketball/2021/12/03/oscar-tshiebwe-gods-guidance-journey-kentucky/ |website=Sports Spectrum |date=3 December 2021 |access-date=4 December 2021}} After Tshiebwe began attending Kennedy Catholic High School, Jeff Kollar and his wife, who live near the school, became his [[legal guardian]]s. Kollar and his wife were previously guardians of brothers Mohamed and [[Sagaba Konate]], who both played basketball for Kennedy Catholic. Sagaba Konate also played college basketball for West Virginia. Tshiebwe is a [[Kentucky Colonel]].{{cite web |title=Famous Colonels |url=https://www.kycolonels.org/famous-colonels/ |access-date=13 January 2023 |website=The Honorable Order of Kentucky Colonels}} ===Business interests=== Tshiebwe has become a leading figure in [[Student athlete compensation|name, image, and likeness]] (NIL) deals, despite being unable to take full advantage of his celebrity due to holding a [[F visa|student visa]]. While he is allowed to sign sponsorship deals, he cannot make paid personal appearances (including autograph signings and commercial shoots) while in the U.S. with that visa status.{{cite web |last=Guilbeau |first=Glenn |date=20 April 2022 |title=Thank You, NIL, Kentucky Is Saying After National Player of Year Oscar Tshiebwe Stays |url=https://www.outkick.com/thank-you-nil-kentucky-is-saying-after-national-player-of-year-oscar-tshiebwe-stays/ |access-date=27 August 2022 |website=OutKick}} Tshiebwe's advisers are currently trying to change his visa status to "[[Alien of extraordinary ability|extraordinary ability]]", which would enable him to fully monetize his celebrity.{{cite web |last=Dorisca |first=Samantha |date=12 August 2022 |title=Kentucky's Oscar Tshiebwe Couldn't Do NIL 'Work' In The U.S. — Now, In The Bahamas, He's Expected To Earn Six Figures In One Week |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/kentuckys-oscar-tshiebwe-couldnt-nil-193839904.html |access-date=27 August 2022 |website=Yahoo Sports}} In August 2022, he was temporarily freed from the restrictions of his visa when the Wildcats went on a week-long preseason exhibition tour to [[the Bahamas]].{{cite web |last=Thompson |first=Tyler |date=12 August 2022 |title=Oscar Tshiebwe making the most of NIL opportunities in Bahamas |url=https://www.on3.com/teams/kentucky-wildcats/news/oscar-tshiebwe-nil-opportunities-bahamas-student-visa-kentucky/ |access-date=27 August 2022 |website=Kentucky Sports Radio}} When the team's plane landed in the Bahamas, Tshiebwe's first phone call was reportedly to his agent, asking "Where do you need me?", and he did promotional work for four companies before fully settling into his hotel room. During the Wildcats' down time on that tour, Tshiebwe made numerous photo shoots and advertising reads, and signed large quantities of memorabilia. Kentucky head coach [[John Calipari]] was apparently unfazed by Tshiebwe's off-court work in the Bahamas, reportedly telling ''[[The Athletic]]'', "He can't do this stuff in the States. Oscar, you weren't there today, but we all get why you're doing what you're doing." By the end of the tour, he had reportedly made $500,000, bringing his total NIL money to $2.75 million in about six months.
